Clinical details: Severe aortic stenosis, type 2 diabetes, peripheral arterial disease. TAVI work-up.

Technique: ECG-gated CT angiography of the aortic root and heart, followed by non-gated CT angiography from the thoracic inlet to the lesser trochanters. 85 ml iohexol 350. DLP 768 mGy·cm.

Findings:

Thoracic aorta: Ascending aorta 35 mm. Arch and descending thoracic aorta of normal calibre. No dissection. Moderate arch atheroma.

Subclavian/axillary arteries: Unremarkable. No significant stenosis.

Abdominal aorta: Infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm, maximum AP diameter 36 mm, with eccentric mural thrombus. Iliac arteries not aneurysmal. Coeliac axis, SMA and renal arteries patent. Ultrasound surveillance in line with NHS AAA Screening Programme intervals is suggested, if appropriate to overall management.

Iliofemoral access (minimal luminal diameter):
Right: CIA 8.0 mm, EIA 6.8 mm, CFA 7.0 mm.
Left: CIA 7.4 mm, EIA 4.9 mm, CFA 6.1 mm.
Calcification: right mild; left external iliac artery circumferential calcification. Tortuosity: moderate on the left. No dissection.

Lungs and airways: No suspicious pulmonary nodule. Dependent atelectasis. Airways patent.

Pleura and pericardium: No pleural or pericardial effusion.

Mediastinum: No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy.

Upper abdomen: Cholelithiasis. Otherwise unremarkable within the limits of an arterial phase study.

Bones: No aggressive osseous lesion. Degenerative change in the thoracolumbar spine.

Conclusion:
1. Iliofemoral access: right favourable (minimal luminal diameter 6.8 mm); left external iliac artery minimal luminal diameter 4.9 mm with circumferential calcification.
2. 36 mm infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm with mural thrombus.

Transfemoral access is likely to be challenging; alternative access may need to be discussed at the heart team meeting.

Annular sizing, valve morphology, coronary ostial heights and aortic root measurements are reported separately in the structural heart report; please refer to that report for valve planning.
